title: Moisture ingress and mould warning signs
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: Victorian Government, Unlicensed asbestos removal ('Updated' label shown; no date); SafeWork NSW, Class B asbestos removal licence (published 12 November 2025; last modified 12 March 2026); WorkSafe Queensland, Asbestos licences (no date shown).
audience: Property manager partner workers who inspect properties for water damage and may find mould
learningOutcomes: Recognise the visible and indirect signs of moisture ingress and mould growth.
Identify the most common moisture sources to be investigated before any finish is changed.
Stop work and refer where growth is extensive, hidden, or disturbed, using safe handling rules.

instruction.heading: Signs that moisture is getting in
instruction.body: Moisture usually shows before mould does. Look for staining that spreads or returns, paint that bubbles or peels in patches, plaster that feels soft or crumbles, skirting that swells, and corners where condensation collects. A musty smell with no visible cause is also a sign. Mould can appear as dark, green, grey or white patches, often where moisture sits: around windows, in bathrooms and laundries, under sinks, in the corners of cold rooms and behind furniture placed against external walls. Record each sign as seen, with its location and time, and do not assume that a clean surface means a dry one.

instruction.heading: Finding the moisture source
instruction.body: Common sources include roof and gutter leaks, failed flashings, window and door seals, plumbing leaks and drips, drainage problems, rising damp at the base of walls, and poor ventilation that lets condensation build up. Work out where the water is coming from before any finish is covered or changed. Painting or sealing over a damp wall hides the evidence and lets the damage continue. Where the source is not clear, refer for a competent assessment and record the observation.

instruction.heading: Safe handling and the limit of this lesson
instruction.body: Do not disturb visible growth. Do not dry brush, dry sand, scrape or use a household vacuum on it, because that releases spores into the air. Do not use high-pressure water on mould, because it can drive growth into the structure. Keep occupants away from the area, especially children, older people and people with breathing conditions, and ventilate only if it is safe to do so. Observation and recording do not need special equipment beyond normal inspection kit. Remediation of mould is not part of this module. Where growth is extensive, hidden behind a finish, or in a ceiling or subfloor space, stop, keep people clear, and refer to a trained, competent worker under the controls in the High-risk cleaning module.

procedure: Record each sign of moisture or growth as seen, with location and time.
Keep occupants and visitors away from the affected area and ventilate only if safe.
Identify the likely moisture source from the building and the leak history, without opening covers or finishes.
Do not disturb visible growth, and do not paint or seal over damp areas.
Stop and refer where growth is extensive, hidden, or the source is unknown.
Record the referral, the protection in place and the owner of the next action.

workedExamples.situation: During an inspection you find dark patches around a window frame in a bedroom, and the window sill shows staining after rain.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should the patches be wiped and painted over to finish the inspection?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The staining after rain suggests the window is letting water in, and the dark patches are likely growth. Do not disturb or paint over them. Record the sign, keep the room clear, and refer the moisture source for competent investigation. Any remediation of the growth goes under the High-risk cleaning module controls, not into a routine clean.

equipmentAndPpe: Torch for checking corners and reveals
Camera or phone for photographs, with consent
Respiratory protection only where the worker is trained for the task that would disturb material

commonErrors.error: Painting over damp or stained walls.
commonErrors.prevention: Find the moisture source and record it. Paint only when the surface is confirmed dry and sound.

commonErrors.error: Wiping or sweeping visible growth with household equipment.
commonErrors.prevention: Do not disturb the growth. Keep people away and refer.

commonErrors.error: Treating a small patch as minor when it may be the sign of a larger hidden problem.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the sign, check for a moisture source, and refer if the extent or source is unknown.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Mould remediation is outside this module. Remediation is covered by the separate High-risk cleaning module, under its controls and warnings. Refer.

Where the work could disturb materials that may contain asbestos, the state asbestos licensing rules apply. Victoria allows unlicensed removal of non-friable material up to 10 square metres in total, and one hour in any period of seven days which is cumulative across all employees; removal above either limit needs a licence, and this lesson does not grant one. New South Wales requires a Class B licence once the area of non-friable material passes 10 square metres (SafeWork NSW, published 12 November 2025, modified 12 March 2026). Queensland needs no licence for non-friable material at or under 10 square metres (WorkSafe Queensland, no date shown).
Completing this lesson does not give a remediation, asbestos or building licence, certificate or authority to perform regulated work.

qualityStandard: Each sign of moisture or growth is recorded as seen, with location and time.
No growth is disturbed, and no damp surface is covered before the source is recorded.
Extensive, hidden or unexplained growth is referred and the referral is recorded.
documentationEvidence: Observation record with location, time and photographs taken with consent
Moisture source note, or a record that the source is unknown
Referral note with the protection in place and the next owner
summary: Moisture shows before mould, so look for staining, bubbling, soft plaster and musty smells.
Find the moisture source before covering or changing any finish.
Do not disturb growth. Refer extensive or hidden growth to the High-risk cleaning controls.

knowledgeChecks.question: Dark patches and staining appear around a window after rain. What is the correct first step?
options: Wipe the patches and paint over them, since the paint hides the marks until the next rain
Dry brush the patches to remove them quickly, then check that the surface is clean and dry
Use high-pressure water to clean the area, since the water will remove the marks
Record the signs, keep the room clear, and refer the moisture source for investigation

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must visible growth not be dry brushed or swept with a household vacuum?
options: It can release spores into the air
It damages the paint and plaster
It leaves a stain on the wall surface
It is only a cosmetic problem

knowledgeChecks.question: What must be done before a finish on a damp wall is covered or changed?
options: Paint over it to hide the stain
Work out where the water is coming from
Seal it with a vapour barrier only
